coding.note: Claims are restricted to the abstract/introduction; Section 3.2 extensions are not separately coded as introductory novelty claims. The identical ELECTRA 15% ablation isolates learning from all positions (Table 5). MULTI refers to repeated fine-tuning, not independent pre-training runs. Comparator provenance is mixed: author-trained BERT baselines and borrowed published results. Token disclosure gives corpus token counts, not an explicit cumulative processed-token total. Data sources are named but mixture proportions are absent. Third-party evaluation is the reported GLUE leaderboard evaluation. Similarities to NCE/CBOW do not explicitly rename those existing techniques.

claims.quote:
As an alternative, we propose replaced token detection, a pre-training task in which the model learns
to distinguish real input tokens from plausible but synthetically generated replacements.
claims.ablation_quote:
This model is identical to ELECTRA except the discriminator loss only
  comes from the 15% of the tokens that were masked out of the input.
claims.claim: Introduce replaced token detection: discriminate original tokens from generator replacements, learning over all input positions.

claims.quote:
Through a series of ablations, we
  show that learning from all input positions causes ELECTRA to train much faster than BERT.
claims.claim: Learning from all positions improves compute efficiency over masked language modeling.

claims.quote:
For example, we build an ELECTRA-Small
  model that can be trained on 1 GPU in 4 days.
claims.claim: Develop a small, accessible model trainable on one GPU in four days that outperforms comparable BERT and larger GPT.

claims.quote:
Our approach also works well at large scale, where we train an ELECTRA-Large
  model that performs comparably to RoBERTa (Liu et al., 2019) and XLNet (Yang et al., 2019), de-
  spite having fewer parameters
claims.claim: Scale ELECTRA to large models, matching RoBERTa/XLNet with fewer parameters and one-quarter the compute, and surpassing them with comparable compute.

claims.quote:
Training ELECTRA-Large
  further results in an even stronger model that outperforms ALBERT (Lan et al., 2019) on GLUE
  and sets a new state-of-the-art for SQuAD 2.0.
claims.claim: Further-trained ELECTRA-Large surpasses ALBERT on GLUE and establishes a new SQuAD 2.0 state of the art.
